item.research_question: What are the phase-specific mechanical behaviors, deformation mechanisms, and phase-boundary interactions in the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy under small-scale loading?
item.material_system: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy (lamellar arrangement of L12 and B2 solid-solution phases)
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc-melting of pure elements (>99.9% purity) with homogenization via multiple flips and re-melting cycles; samples polished to 0.02 µm roughness; micro-pillars prepared via FIB (30 kV Ga+ down to 5 kV) with final diameter 2.0 ± 0.3 µm and aspect ratio ~2; bulk specimens prepared via EDM (tensile) and machining (compression)
item.test_conditions: Bulk tensile/compression at 10^-3 s^-1; nano-indentation at 10000 µN and 500 µN loads; strain rate sensitivity at 4×10^-2, 1.2×10^-1, and 4×10^-1 s^-1; micro-pillar compression at ~2.5×10^-4 s^-1; scratch tests at 500 mN load with ramping to 3000 µN
key_findings: Ultimate tensile strength of 1165 ± 20 MPa with ~18% elongation; ultimate compressive strength of 1863 ± 12 MPa with ~34% fracture strain.
B2 phase showed higher hardness (7.5 ± 2.2 GPa at 500 µN) compared to L12 phase (6.0 ± 0.5 GPa).
B2 phase exhibited higher strain rate sensitivity (SRS) than L12, with bulk SRS close to B2 values.
Micro-pillar yield strength was ~610 MPa for B2 and ~460 MPa for L12; mixed pillars showed double yielding at ~350 MPa and ~620-640 MPa.
B2 phase deformed via plastic barreling with limited slip steps, while L12 phase showed high density of slip steps and homogeneous flow.
Coefficient of friction was ~0.89 for B2 and ~0.83 for L12; L12 showed more material pile-up during scratch tests.
Phase boundary remained preserved without separation or cracking even after high compressive strains in mixed micro-pillars.
item.mechanism: The B2 phase controls deformation due to its higher strength and SRS, while the L12 phase accommodates plasticity through multiple slip systems. The semi-coherent phase boundary prevents crack propagation and separation, contributing to high strength and ductility. Cr-rich nano-precipitates (~20 nm) in the B2 phase act as barriers to dislocation movement, enhancing strength. The tension-compression asymmetry arises from lamellar orientation, elastic property differences, and volume fractions of the phases.
item.limitations: The study notes that multiple yield points were not detected in bulk tests likely due to the small difference in modulus between phases and lower resolution of bulk experiments. The anisotropic behavior may depend on the location of samples due to varying cooling conditions in the ingot.
item.future_work: The authors state these results will pave the way for fundamental understanding of phase-specific contributions to bulk mechanical response and help in designing structural materials with high fracture toughness.
quotes: Dual mode fracture was observed with ductile failure for L12 phase and brittle mode for B2 phase.
